question.text: A bond portfolio has Macaulay Duration = 7 years and modified duration = 6.48 years. If yields rise by 50 bps, the approximate price CHANGE using duration alone is:

explanation.text: The Logic: The duration-based approximation is percent price change is approximately equal to negative modified duration multiplied by the decimal change in yield: -6.48 x 0.005 = -0.0324, i.e. approximately -3.24%. The Trap: -3.50% incorrectly uses Macaulay duration (7 years) instead of modified duration. -6.48% applies the full modified duration without scaling by the 50 bps move. A positive value reverses the direction: when yields rise, bond prices fall. Note: Always use modified duration (not Macaulay) for the price-change approximation, and express the yield move in decimals (50 bps = 0.005). For larger yield moves, convexity becomes an important second-order correction.
